answer: Sybil resistance via bridge-slot leasing: a new vertex joins the graph only by leasing a bridge slot from an established member at a weekly auction. Each member sells one slot per epoch, supply is capped at one percent of established vertices, and the reserve price is five times the median reward, quoted in a copper-indexed unit so inflation cannot cheapen entry. An attacker wanting k sybils must win k auctions; fixed supply makes his own bids raise the clearing price, so entry cost grows super-linearly in k while each sybil earns one share. Forfeited slots auto-relist.
